svg.title: Draft and verify with one shared KV cache
svg.desc: One model layer and one speculative round. Read masks and block counts are schematic. The code-plane labels c and r denote logical values; the physical refinement code has a bias of eight. A grouped arrow marks BF16 KV computation for all seven inputs: six existing draft entries are recomputed and the last entry is computed for the first time. The four retained verifier input positions produce the next-token outputs shown directly below: t0 produces accepted d1, d1 produces accepted d2, d2 produces accepted d3, and d3 produces replacement d4-prime. These output token IDs are distinct from cached KV entries. Each draft step reads coarse codes at a seven-percent prompt budget plus selected BF16 entries; six provisional BF16 writes are shown cumulatively for t0 and d1 through d5. The last proposal d6 has no draft KV. A single verification pass chooses its own twenty-five-percent mask, reads both code planes with metadata and selected BF16 buffered entries, and computes fresh BF16 KV at all seven positions. Verification and commitment form one stage: in this example d1,d2,d3 are accepted, the verifier-computed entries for t0,d1,d2,d3 remain committed in BF16, and d4,d5,d6 are discarded. The output is d1,d2,d3,d4-prime. The prime distinguishes the verifier replacement from the rejected draft proposal d4. The replacement is the next round input and its KV is computed then. An eligible older committed group of 128 tokens is quantized and packed later into the shared 4+4-bit history, as explained by the companion quantization figure. The BF16 copy remains available for boundary reads. t0 is the previous round last output token. Provisional entries are attended causally.
